notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents covering 2026-10-11/12. Routine EGRESS_BLOCKED/ENOTFOUND on nearly every org-domain WebFetch attempt (anthropic.com/news being the one exception, which fetched cleanly and showed nothing newer than Oct 8, already filed); all four lanes worked around this via WebSearch. Same-day (Oct 11-12) announcement coverage was thin to empty across all four lanes - no lane found a quotable, well-sourced same-day item, so this run files zero `announcement`-kind entries, same pattern as the 2026-10-10 run. The calendar is dense (620 entries going in) so most forward-looking candidates each lane surfaced were cross-checked by the lanes themselves against what they already knew was filed; this findings file keeps the genuinely new or better-sourced ones plus a handful of re-affirmations of existing confirmed data (left for the apply script to merge/refresh rather than skip).
concerns: The security lane could not find any fresh (Oct 11/12) same-day CVE/breach announcement with quotable body-text sourcing despite ~15 targeted queries - KEV catalog and breach trackers searched all lag by several days. This may be a systematic gap in how well this routine can cover same-day security news through search alone; worth checking if a direct cisa.gov fetch ever succeeds in a future run's environment.

The devtools/cloud lane flagged that AWS Lambda's deprecated-runtime block-create/block-update dates (nodejs20.x, nodejs18.x, python3.8/3.9, ruby3.2, dotnet6) have reportedly shifted at least once in AWS's own docs per secondary sources; filed at 'expected' rather than 'confirmed' since the live AWS runtimes page could not be fetched directly - a maintainer with working fetch access to docs.aws.amazon.com should verify the Feb 1 / Mar 3 2027 dates directly.

The bigtech/hardware lane could not resolve conflicting dates for Samsung Galaxy Unpacked 2027 and MWC Las Vegas 2026 (one source puts MWC Las Vegas in June 2026, another implies October by analogy with the 2024 edition) and left both out rather than guess - a maintainer with better source access could pin these down.

ASML, SK hynix, and Broadcom Q3/Q4 2026 earnings dates filed this run come only from third-party financial calendars (MarketScreener/TipRanks/days.to), not the companies' own investor pages, which were unreachable via WebFetch - filed at 'expected' confidence pending direct confirmation from a maintainer with working access to those investor-relations pages.

The AI lane noticed a secondary source giving Jan 20, 2027 for what may be the same OpenAI legacy audio/realtime model retirement already filed as 'rumored' with a Jan 6, 2027 date (openai-retires-tts-1-tts-1-hd-and-gpt-4o-mini-tts-2027-01) - worth a maintainer's direct re-check against developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations.

EU AI Act's Annex III (standalone high-risk systems) compliance deadline was pushed from Aug 2, 2026 to Dec 2, 2027, and Annex I (embedded high-risk systems) to Aug 2, 2028, under the Digital Omnibus - both fall beyond today's 12-month write window so were not filed; flagging per the run instructions for pickup once the window reaches them.

Oracle's own blog lists further confirmed CPU/CSPU dates beyond this run's near-term focus (CSPU 2026-11-17, 2026-12-15; CPU 2027-01-19, 2027-04-20, 2027-07-20) - not filed this run since they're routine recurring dates outside the immediate window, but worth a future run picking them up as the window advances.

Standing issue, not introduced this run (flagged in multiple prior runs' concerns, still unresolved): data/events/2027-01.json still carries three near-duplicate entries for the same Google Play Contacts/Location/SMS policy change, all dated 2027-01-27, plus a geofencing-removal detail from developer.android.com/distribute/play-policies that none of the three capture. A maintainer should merge these and fold in the geofencing detail.

Introduced and then fixed within this run: my first pass at filing the Let's Encrypt 64-day-certificate finding created a genuine third near-duplicate rather than merging ('let-s-encrypt-isrg-let-s-encrypt-default-certificates-shorte-2027-02' against the existing 'let-s-encrypt-default-profile-switches-to-64-day-certificate-2027-02', both 2027-02-10, same fact) — the exact sameTitle-miss pattern flagged in the 2026-10-08 run's concerns (shared tokens 'default'+'64' land well under the 0.6 Jaccard floor). Caught it by diffing the applied data before committing. Fixed it properly rather than leaving a third row: re-filed the new source (isrg.org) under the existing entry's exact title so it merged into that record, and re-filed the duplicate's own title/org/date with status:'superseded' so the row is retired rather than visible on the public calendar. A maintainer should still consider whether sameTitle needs a lower floor or synonym handling, since this is now confirmed across at least two separate runs' entries.

Introduced and then root-caused and fixed within this run: filing the Apple CEO-succession finding first created a second entry for a fact already on file since 2026-08-20 (data/events/2026-09.json already had 'apple-tim-cook-becomes-apple-executive-chairman-john-ternus-2026-09', sourced directly to apple.com/newsroom). Traced why src/lib/id.ts's isSameThing missed this one even though the two titles share 8 of 9 distinctive tokens (well over the 0.6 floor): titleTokens() calls slugify() on the full title BEFORE splitting into tokens, and slugify() truncates to 60 characters. Both titles are long enough that the truncation lands mid-word — the existing title's slug cuts 'becomes-ceo' down to '...john-ternus-becom' (losing 'ceo', corrupting 'becomes' into 'become'), mine cuts '...executive-chairman' down to '...executive-ch'. The corrupted trailing tokens no longer match, dropping shared-token count below threshold. This is the mechanism behind the vague 'slug-truncation' issue flagged in several prior runs' concerns (the ICLR 2027 duplicate pair and others) — now confirmed with a reproducible cause. Caught it by diffing the applied data before committing, and fixed it the same way: re-filed my two sources under the existing entry's exact title so they merged into that record, and re-filed my own title/org/date with status:'superseded' to retire the duplicate row. I did not touch src/lib/id.ts itself — application code is out of scope for this routine — but a maintainer should move the 60-char truncation so it only applies when deriving the id string, not when tokenizing a title for comparison; left as written, any pair of long, token-overlapping titles can fail to merge this same way.

Tooling note for future runs and maintainers, discovered this run: scripts/apply-findings.ts fully overwrites data/runs/<date>.json on every invocation rather than merging across calls in the same session. I called it three times today (full apply, then two correction passes after catching the two duplicates above via validate:data/git diff), so the on-disk run log's 'added'/'updated' arrays reflect only the diff from my final call (0 added, 4 updated), not the day's real net effect. The true tally for 2026-10-12, reconciled by hand from each call's console output, is +8 new live entries, ~22 updated, 0 pruned, plus 2 entries filed and retired (status:superseded) in the same run. A maintainer relying solely on the run log file to gauge a run's productivity should know multiple same-day apply calls will undercount 'added' this way; the commit message for today's run states the reconciled totals instead of the file's.
